title: SQL: DDL and DML — CREATE, ALTER, DROP, INSERT, SELECT, UPDATE, DELETE

learning_objectives.text: define data types in an SQL database
compare data definition language (DDL) and data manipulation language (DML)
create a database structure using DDL commands: CREATE, ALTER and DROP
use SQL SELECT, UPDATE, INSERT and DELETE queries to manage data in a single table

lesson_objectives.all: tell DDL from DML, choose SQL data types and write CREATE TABLE, INSERT and a simple SELECT … WHERE that run in the SQL runner
lesson_objectives.most: change a table's structure with ALTER and DROP and manage records with UPDATE and DELETE using a correct WHERE condition
lesson_objectives.some: write tables with foreign, unique and composite keys and queries with AND, LIKE and IS NULL, and explain why UPDATE / DELETE without WHERE is dangerous

assessment_criteria.criterion: Create a database structure with DDL
descriptors: chooses suitable data types (INT, VARCHAR(n), CHAR(n), DECIMAL(p,s), DATE, BOOLEAN)
writes CREATE TABLE with a primary key and constraints; changes it with ALTER TABLE … ADD / DROP COLUMN; removes a table with DROP TABLE

assessment_criteria.criterion: Manage data in a single table with DML
descriptors: adds records with INSERT INTO … VALUES
selects fields and records with SELECT … FROM … WHERE (comparison, AND, LIKE, IS NULL)
changes and deletes the right records with UPDATE … SET … WHERE and DELETE FROM … WHERE

learners_can: read an SQL statement aloud and say what it does
explain the difference between DDL and DML in one sentence
describe an error message and how they fixed it
phrases: This statement is DDL / DML because it changes the structure / the data …

values.action: Learners run their code, read the error messages and correct it until the SQL runner accepts it.
Every learner writes and runs their own statements; the teacher sees each attempt live.
Learners build on their ERDs and data dictionaries and see the same SQL used in real systems (school, library, shop).

cross_curricular: English: technical vocabulary and precise instructions.
Mathematics: comparison operators and conditions (>, <, BETWEEN, AND).
ict: ICT Practice Platform, Lessons section: theory as slides, live votes, tasks pushed to every learner's screen.
SQL runner: learners run their code on a sample database, see the result table and the tables after their code; Check Answer marks it automatically.
Teacher → Lessons shows every learner's answers and marks live.
previous_learning: Basic concepts of a database (tables, fields, records, keys, data types), ERDs, the data dictionary and normalisation.

blocks.title: Hook: who talks to the database?
blocks.teacher: Shows the lesson objectives and asks how the school's e-journal stores and changes marks.
blocks.learners: Vote and give one example of data that is added, changed or deleted in a school system.

poll.question: A teacher corrects a mark in the e-journal. What does the system do to the database?
options: Changes a record in an existing table
Nothing — marks are stored on paper

blocks.title: Starter: DDL or DML?
blocks.teacher: Pushes three practice questions; shows the class results and clears up the most common wrong answer.
blocks.learners: Sort the commands into DDL and DML, complete the definition of DML and match each command with its purpose.
resources: Practice: DDL or DML, The term DML, What each command does

blocks.title: Slides: data types and DDL
blocks.teacher: Explains SQL, DDL vs DML, the data types and CREATE / ALTER / DROP with the slides; writes CREATE TABLE Students live in the SQL runner and runs it, then shows a common error (missing comma, text without quotes).
blocks.learners: Follow the slides, answer the votes, say which data type fits each field.
slides: What SQL is: DDL and DML
Creating the structure: CREATE, ALTER, DROP
resources: Theory slides: What SQL is, Data types, CREATE / ALTER / DROP
Live votes: Choosing SQL data types, Find the error

blocks.title: SQL runner: create and change tables
blocks.teacher: Pushes the DDL tasks; walks round, helps learners read error messages ("Show the database", "Run SQL") and shows one good solution on the board after each two tasks.
blocks.learners: Write each statement in the SQL runner, run it, look at the tables after the code, correct errors, then press Check Answer. Fast finishers do the foreign-key and unique tasks.
resources: SQL runner tasks (practice): create tables, add / remove a column, delete a table

blocks.title: Slides: INSERT, SELECT, UPDATE, DELETE
blocks.teacher: Explains DML with the slides and runs each command live on the Students table; shows what happens to the table when UPDATE or DELETE has no WHERE.
blocks.learners: Predict the result of each query before it runs; answer the votes.
slides: Adding and selecting data: INSERT and SELECT
Changing and deleting data: UPDATE and DELETE
resources: Theory slides: INSERT and SELECT, UPDATE and DELETE
Live votes: Which rows are returned?, WHERE operators

blocks.title: SQL runner: manage the data
blocks.teacher: Pushes the DML tasks in order (INSERT → SELECT → UPDATE → DELETE); follows the marks live, stops the class once to discuss the most common error, supports learners who are stuck.
blocks.learners: Write, run and check each query; compare the result table with what the task asks. Fast finishers do LIKE, IS NULL and the composite-key task.
resources: SQL runner tasks (practice): insert, select, update, delete
Slide: the order SELECT → FROM → WHERE and the WHERE operators

blocks.title: Exit ticket
blocks.teacher: Pushes three short practice questions and checks the results to plan the next lesson.
blocks.learners: Complete the CREATE TABLE, the INSERT and the DELETE statements.
resources: Practice: Create the Movies table, Insert a publisher, Delete old books

blocks.title: Reflection and homework
blocks.teacher: Asks the reflection question and sets homework: the remaining practice questions of lesson 1 and handwritten notes of the lesson.
blocks.learners: Vote and name one SQL error they made today and how they fixed it.

poll.question: How confident are you writing SQL statements now?
options: I can write all of them without help
I can write most, but I check the syntax
I need more practice with the SQL runner

safety: Laptops on the desk, charging cables kept off the walkways.
The SQL runner uses a practice database that is reset after every run — nothing real can be damaged.

support: The syntax of each command stays on the slide during the tasks (CREATE TABLE, INSERT INTO … VALUES, SELECT … FROM … WHERE, UPDATE … SET … WHERE, DELETE FROM … WHERE).
"Show the database" lets learners see the table and its field names before they write a query.
Tasks go from simple to harder; the teacher helps learners read error messages one to one.
stretch: Extra SQL runner tasks: foreign keys, UNIQUE, composite primary key, LIKE and IS NULL.
Explain to a neighbour why UPDATE or DELETE without WHERE is dangerous and how to test the WHERE with a SELECT first.

assessment: Starter and exit ticket: automatic marks, seen live by the teacher.
SQL runner tasks: the code runs on a sample database and Check Answer compares the result with a model solution.
Live votes during the slides show misconceptions straight away.
Oral feedback while the teacher walks round; notes checked later against the checklist.
reflection: Could every learner write and run CREATE TABLE, INSERT and SELECT on their own?
Which SQL errors were most common, and what should be repeated next lesson?
Was the time for the SQL runner tasks enough?
